name: Persistence Decay and Forgetting Law
purpose: Define weakening, erosion, and forgetting of reinforced continuation structures.

candidate_law_statement.informal: Persistence is not eternal. Stabilized continuation structures weaken when reinforcement history is no longer renewed or when budget, accessibility, perturbation, or reconstruction conditions degrade.

formal.reinforcement_erosion_condition: Erode(C_P) occurs when Reinforce(C_P,n+1) < Reinforce(C_P,n) under decay tolerance λ.
formal.forgetting_condition: Forget(C_P) occurs when H(C_P,n) falls below reconstruction or reinforcement accessibility threshold.
formal.basin_weakening_condition: Weaken(B_U) occurs when admissibility margin, reinforcement inflow, or accessibility coherence declines below basin persistence tolerance.
formal.transient_lawlike_clause: Law-like channels may be temporary, metastable, or locally valid rather than eternal.
formal.nonprimitive_memory_clause: Forgetting is loss of accessible reinforcement continuity, not destruction of a primitive memory substance.
